literatureReviews.resourceInsights: Offloading secondary UI (maps, stats) to peripheral devices (smartwatch/AR) reduces cognitive load on the primary screen. This allows the mobile phone to focus purely on gameplay while the AR headset expands the "visual real-estate."
literatureReviews.comments: This supports the "Second Screen" feature. The user stays focused on the phone while the AR headset provides a dashboard in the physical space.

literatureReviews.resourceInsights: Smartwatches are best for 2-4 second interactions. In gaming, this is ideal for quick stat checks notifications that don't require the player to look away from the main screen for long.
literatureReviews.comments: Use the Smartwatch component for "Pulse" notifications—quick vibrates and 1-second glances at stats.

literatureReviews.resourceName: Managing Attention Fragmentation in Multi-Screen Play
literatureReviews.resourceInsights: Too many screens can lead to "Attention Split." The UI must be hierarchical: Action (Phone) > Strategy (AR) > Status (Watch).
literatureReviews.comments: Gamar must ensure that the AR headset isn't too busy, or the user will get overwhelmed and take it off.

literatureReviews.resourceInsights: Headsets provide Spatial Audio which, when paired with AR visuals, creates a 360-degree information field. Research suggests that audio cues can effectively direct a user's eyes to a specific part of the AR overlay or the Smartwatch.
literatureReviews.comments: Since the user uses a headset, GAMAR should use 3D audio to tell them where to look
